fr:title.text: Figure out direnv + git worktrees without blowing up the nix store

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Figure out direnv + git worktrees without blowing up the nix store

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Agentic programming on multiple feature branches is most natural with one git worktree per branch plus direnv for an automatic Nix dev shell per directory. But each .direnv becomes a GC root that pins its full flake-input closure, and these accumulate — the April 2026 cleanup found 157 direnv-originated GC roots across 11 project dirs in ~, most of them stale.
Goal. A workflow where I can freely spin up worktrees for agent sessions and let direnv auto-load shells, without the nix store growing unboundedly.

html:ul.html:li: Periodic sweep: find ~ -maxdepth 3 -type d -name .direnv -atime +N -print and delete stale ones.
On worktree removal: auto-run rm -rf .direnv first so GC roots drop immediately (git hook or wrapper around git worktree remove).
Shared flake-inputs cache at a stable path so multiple worktrees of the same repo reuse one closure instead of pinning N copies.
nix-direnv TTL / age-out settings — verify current behavior and whether a shorter cache window makes the closure-pinning less painful.
direnv allow gating: only allow direnv in active worktrees; require explicit re-allow when returning to a dormant one.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Context. See automatic nix store maintenance for the baseline GC/optimise config that should be in place regardless of the strategy chosen here.

Without explicit configuration, a nix-darwin store grows monotonically: every darwin-rebuild switch or home-manager switch pins its closure as a rooted generation, and nothing ages out. Three settings in configuration.nix prevent this.
Scheduled GC + optimise. Runs on a timer; --delete-older-than keeps enough rollback history to be useful without hoarding ancient generations.

Build-time dedup and emergency GC. auto-optimise-store hardlinks identical files as they arrive in the store, so duplication never accumulates — avoiding the multi-hour nix store optimise of a 48G store (which on APFS can freeze the machine). min-free/max-free triggers GC during builds when the data volume runs low, so a build never fails for want of space.
The bigger recurring lever in practice is direnv/worktree hygiene — see the open question.
